evals.name: saucedemo-purchase-journey
evals.prompt: demo the Swag Labs store at https://www.saucedemo.com to the QA candidates at 4 — signing in, sorting the products by price, adding two items to the cart, and finishing checkout. one window, step by step so they can follow.
evals.expected_output: A demo-<date>.md plan with a beat-sheet section per named feature, credentials and checkout data staged as fixtures, tab group defined, tempo, teardown and per-feature off-script recovery; presentation held for approval.
assertions: Writes a dated demo plan file (demo-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md) as a single artifact rather than only answering in prose
Plan carries a beat sheet with one section per feature named in the request
Every beat names exactly one browser interaction plus the element it targets
Every beat carries narration written as the words to be spoken, not a description of what to say
Every fixture the beats touch has a written creation step or a stated source
Plan states a teardown or reset path back to the pre-demo state
Plan gives a per-feature recovery for the demo going off-script live
Plan defines the Chrome tab group by name and lists its tabs in load order
Plan specifies human-paced pauses with concrete durations between actions
Toolbelt lists the browser tool names actually found in this session, each with the job it does
Element targets are grounded in what the live page shows rather than guessed labels
Holds back from presenting and puts the plan to the user for approval first
Beat sheet covers all four named features: sign in, sort by price, add two items, complete checkout
Login credentials are staged as a fixture with their source named, not invented
Checkout form data (first name, last name, postal code) is specified in advance

evals.name: saucedemo-failure-paths
evals.prompt: show the team the unhappy paths on https://www.saucedemo.com — the locked out user hitting the wall, and a checkout that gets rejected because the postal code is blank. want them to see the actual error messages.
evals.expected_output: A plan covering both failure paths, with the expected error text as each beat's Confirm, and a stated distinction between an error the demo means to show and the demo going off-script.
